established_findings.statement: LLMs can be used to translate high-level network intents into low-level network configurations or code, but achieved correctness varies across tasks and settings.
limitations: Reported results derive from research prototypes, benchmarks, or surveys rather than broad production deployments.
Performance depends on model, prompt, fine-tuning, and dataset specifics not uniformly controlled across studies.

established_findings.statement: Hallucination, factual errors, and prompt sensitivity are common failure modes for LLMs and materially affect reliability for operational tasks.
limitations: Most analyses quantify hallucination and prompt-sensitivity in general LLM tasks; transfer to specific NetOps failure rates requires domain-specific measurement.

established_findings.statement: Architectures that combine generation, automated validation (deterministic or formal validators), and iterative repair improve reliability of model-produced artifacts in safety-critical domains.
limitations: Demonstrations are domain-specific (e.g., PLC, cybersecurity RAG) and vary in verifier strength; direct transfer to NetOps requires integration with network-specific validators (reachability, ACL equivalence).

established_findings.statement: Tool-using and multi-agent LLM frameworks enable more complex NetOps-like workflows but introduce multi-turn safety and governance risks that require explicit mitigation (confidence gating, human-in-the-loop, contracts/auditable loops).
limitations: Risk assessments are mostly conceptual or benchmark-based; operational effectiveness of specific governance measures in deployed NetOps remains under-evaluated.

established_findings.statement: Evaluation and benchmark practices for LLMs face validity threats (dataset contamination, benchmark fragility), which can inflate perceived capabilities if not controlled.
limitations: While general benchmark vulnerabilities are well-documented, the degree of contamination or inflation for specific NetOps benchmarks needs per-dataset analysis.

established_findings.statement: Confidence estimation and calibration methods exist but no single method is uniformly reliable across tasks; calibrated uncertainty can help gating but remains imperfect.
limitations: Calibration experiments are often on NLP or QA benchmarks; applying them to structured NetOps outputs (configs, ACLs) may require different scoring/verification approaches.

unresolved_questions.statement: To what extent do LLM-generated network configurations, validated by automated network-specific validators, succeed when executed on real network devices under realistic topologies and failure conditions?
limitations: Existing papers demonstrate intent→config translation and generator–validator concepts but few published experiments execute validated outputs on real device testbeds with systematic failure injection.

unresolved_questions.statement: How much evaluation inflation in NetOps-oriented benchmarks stems from training-data contamination for contemporary LLMs?
limitations: Surveys document contamination risks generally; quantifying contamination requires dataset-level membership tests or mechanistic methods (not present in the supplied NetOps records).

unresolved_questions.statement: Which concrete verifier types (formal reachability, ACL equivalence, simulation/emulation) and verification strengths are necessary to reduce catastrophic NetOps actions to acceptable operational risk?
limitations: Papers propose verification components but do not converge on a validated minimal verifier set for production NetOps safety.

unresolved_questions.statement: How robust are prompt-hardening, few-shot exemplars, or structured prompting strategies specifically for NetOps tasks across model families and prompt-coupling effects?
limitations: General prompt-sensitivity analyses exist but domain-specific systematic studies for NetOps prompts across multiple models are lacking in the supplied records.

unresolved_questions.statement: What human-in-the-loop gating policies (confidence thresholds, review workflows) provide best trade-offs between automation benefit and operational safety in NetOps agentic workflows?
limitations: Papers recommend HITL and gating concepts; empirical comparisons of specific gating thresholds/workflows for NetOps are not provided in these records.

unresolved_questions.statement: Can calibrated model-confidence signals reliably predict semantic correctness of structured network artifacts (e.g., ACL semantics, routing policies) before execution?
limitations: Calibration work mainly covers QA; mapping token-level confidence to semantic correctness of configurations remains an open empirical question.

candidate_gaps.statement: Absence of publicly verified NetOps evaluation suites that combine intent→configuration tasks with executable device-level testbed runs, deterministic formal validators, and contamination controls.
limitations: NetConfEval and related task suites exist but supplied records do not document a combined, contamination-controlled, device-execution benchmark covering validators and testbeds.

candidate_gaps.statement: Limited demonstrated integration of network-domain formal-method validators (reachability/ACL equivalence) into LLM generation–verify–repair loops in published NetOps work.
limitations: Some papers propose verification components conceptually; concrete integrations with network formal validators and empirical results are sparse in the supplied set.

candidate_gaps.statement: Insufficient empirical studies measuring multi-turn agent safety degradation and mitigation effectiveness specifically for NetOps multi-step workflows.
limitations: Multi-turn safety benchmarks exist in other domains; the supplied records do not present extensive NetOps-specific multi-turn safety evaluations.

candidate_gaps.statement: Lack of domain-specific methods mapping model confidence/calibration to deterministic semantic checks for network configuration correctness.
limitations: Calibration literature is general; conversion into reliable semantic gating metrics for structured NetOps outputs is not demonstrated in supplied records.

candidate_gaps.statement: Few publicly available, contamination-audited NetOps datasets with provenance to support honest evaluation of LLM capabilities in the domain.
limitations: Some datasets and benchmarks exist, but supplied records highlight contamination risks and call for provenance controls; explicit audited NetOps datasets are not evident in the provided set.

candidate_gaps.statement: Limited published work on end-to-end cost/reliability trade-offs for closed-loop NetOps agent architectures (verification latency, loop cost, catastrophic-action rate) tailored to networks.
limitations: Architectural proposals and metrics (e.g., WoI) exist, but network-specialized experimental evaluations quantifying trade-offs are not present in the supplied records.

excluded_claims: Claims that LLM-based NetOps systems are production-ready and safe for unsupervised deployment — not supported by the supplied empirical/survey records.
Any assertion of comprehensive superiority of a specific LLM or agent framework across NetOps tasks without multi-model, contamination-controlled comparisons — unsupported by provided records.
Fabricated performance numbers (e.g., device-level success rates on live networks) not present in the supplied record set.
